subject: Differences between estimated and observed genetic map

messages.author: f843dbdb315d5670
messages.subject: Differences between estimated and observed genetic map
parts:
Hello,
I would like to know the possible reasons why I am getting almost 10 times differences between estimated and observed genetic map of my tomato introgression lines. Value ranges of estimated genetic map shows just up to 15-20 cM for each chromosome size while the real ones are of ca.100 cM.
Thanks for any help and advice.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Differences between estimated and observed genetic map
parts:
Hard to tell from the limited information you provide, but my guess would be that you’re getting biased estimates of genetic distances with your introgression lines. And I’m not sure how one would estimate a genetic map from data on introgression lines.

karl

Dear Karl,
Thanks for kind reply. In fact these first generation 50 ILs cover the whole genome of wild type donor (S. pennelli). The segments are overlapped in each chromosome and there was no gap on genotype part because I filled BB for all segments as donor's genotype and AA for all free space of the entire genome as the recurrent background. Above from them I filled the genotype of donor as BB and that of mother (recurrent) as AA. I did this as a normal step to compare with observed one. If I don't need to do this for ILs, it would be wonderful. But I doubt that the way I put the genotypic symbol in the dataset might have problem because it showed strange values of R2 (e.g 4000) when I did X2 test. By the way I repeat the whole dataset of phenotype 4 times as replications. I would be grateful if you help me out. If you want to see my data set. I can send you.
Great thanks.
